Terra Bellum — Bezel UI, full demo

The brass-instrument direction taken across the game's main functions. Everything is interactive: M move · N nations · B budget · D decrees · C council · A annals · G goals · Esc close · Enter end turn. Click departments of France, drag the budget knobs, hold the war button.

Shape rules (what changed from the first draft)

  • Round = instrument, notched rectangle = document. Dials, gauges, rail keys, minimap, knobs, End Turn, the map ring are bezels. Panels, tags and tooltips are rectangles with cut corners and a hairline. No rounded-rectangle cards anywhere.
  • One ornament: the graduated rule under every header, the same tick grammar as the bezel scales and the tuner.
  • State is carried by the instrument, not by tinted boxes: gauge arc length and colour, relation arc around a flag, needle on a knob, fill on a hold button, ring on a goal.
  • Colour: brass is the accent; rust = danger/attention; verdigris = good; sky = info/allied. Figures are lining numerals in Alegreya; labels are wide-tracked Cinzel caps.
  • One icon set (40 glyphs, 24-px grid, 1.7 stroke) drawn for this UI, shown in the kit.

Phone 390×844

The top row keeps three gauges; End Turn is a raised chronometer in a notched bottom dock; the radial ring becomes a hub on the map with a bottom sheet for verbs; screens are full-height sheets.

Open questions

  • Radial ring on touch: the phone version uses a sheet of four round keys instead. Do you want the ring on phones too?
  • Stat-heavy screens (budget, nations) stay dark. A light "document" panel (like the Almanac page) could be an option for long reading screens such as Annals.
  • Brass bevels: kept to a single highlight arc + shaded arc to stay cheap in Godot (drawn arcs and ticks, no textures).
